data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English 'mærh' meaning 'meadow' and 'hlaw' meaning 'hill' or 'warrior'. Marlow may refer to a warrior who lived near a meadow or a meadow that was a battlefield. The name Marlow carries the meaning “Meadow warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Marlow usually hope their child will grow to embody meadow warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The name also implies the warrior's connection to nature, as both a meadow and a hill are associated with the natural world. It can serve as a reminder to courageously stand up for what is right, even in the face of challenges or obstacles.
